SAT Test Builder

Build SAT Math or Reading and Writing tests from SAT question-bank PDF, then download them for offline practice.

Your PDF stays in your browser. Each test has two timed modules, with answers and explanations for review.

Quick start

  1. Open the Educator Question Bank in a new tab. Choose SAT, one subject and all domains.
  2. Optionally check Exclude Active Questions to avoid questions from official practice tests. Choose Manage Selection → Select Entire Set, then Export → With correct answers and explanations → Export PDF.
  3. Choose that PDF below, review the recommended test counts and generate your tests. Download them for offline practice.

The available questions may limit coverage. You can change any count or use 0 to skip a bucket. M1 and M2 include all three difficulty levels; M2 has fewer Easy and more Hard questions than M1. All buckets aim for SAT content balance.

The collection ZIP includes unused questions as separate Easy, Medium and Hard browsing sets. Empty sets are omitted. Counts refer to usable, unique questions; questions are never repeated across tests or unused sets.

Review the counts above, then generate your collection.

No upload, account, or internet connection required. PDF processing happens in this browser. Large question banks can take several minutes. Images are prepared as you preview or download tests.

The distribution we aim for

Difficulty and skill targets are practice defaults. These are fixed practice modules, not adaptive SAT modules. Recommendations aim for all four test difficulties: Easy 15%, Par 35%, Hard 35%, Extra hard 15%. Your chosen counts keep the same fixed difficulty targets, with content balanced within them. A limited bank may miss content targets; every test and report shows actual coverage.

NEXT STEP · PREVIEW OR DOWNLOAD

Browse a test now, or download it to practice offline.

The collection ZIP includes any full tests and unused questions, grouped by difficulty. Extract it, then open index.html or any included HTML file to practice offline.

Every test has two modules: 22 questions each for Math, 27 for Reading and Writing. Check the original images and extracted answers below. Preparing all downloads can take several minutes for a large PDF.

Creating tests and practicing offline

Help · Creating tests and practicing offline

Export your PDF

Open the Educator Question Bank in a new tab. Choose SAT, one subject and all domains. Optionally check Exclude Active Questions to leave out official practice-test questions. Choose Manage Selection → Select Entire Set, then Export → With correct answers and explanations → Export PDF.

Build and download

Choose one PDF up to 300 MB. Review excluded questions and the recommended full-test counts: one of each bucket when possible, then Easy 15%, Par 35%, Hard 35%, Extra hard 15%. Edit any count, use 0 to skip a bucket, or restore the recommendation. If questions are short, reduce the counts. Changing counts or choosing a new PDF clears generated tests from the page; files already downloaded are unaffected.

Generate and preview your tests, then download an HTML file or the collection ZIP. Extract the ZIP and open index.html or an individual HTML file in a browser with JavaScript enabled. Questions, images, answers and explanations work offline. Unused questions come in separate Easy, Medium and Hard browsing sets.

Save and resume

Use Pause before leaving a timed test; switching tabs does not stop the timer. Browser saves may be lost if you move or rename files, clear browser data, or use private browsing. Choose Save unfinished attempt to download a portable copy, then open it and choose Continue saved test. Use the newest copy; copies do not sync. After finishing, download your results report. Browsing is untimed.

Keep in mind

These are fixed practice modules with raw scores, not adaptive SAT tests or scaled scores. PDFs are processed locally. Large exports can take several minutes; use Cancel or Try again, or download individual tests if needed. Math uses images with limited screen-reader access. Downloaded files contain the PDF filename, source questions and answers; saved attempts also include your responses. Use and share source material only as its owner permits.
